lot: Lot 4 - Coordinator Reliability, Recovery & Supervisor Agent

priority_mapping.0: P0 / Not parallel-safe — must run alone

assumptions: The coordinator codebase is Rust and follows the existing module layout under core/src/coordinator/.
Error codes E100-E900 already exist and new sub-codes must stay within this taxonomy.
The worker pool model (reusable worktree slots) is unchanged; improvements refine how slots are reused and retried.
IPC between coordinator and performers uses the existing events.jsonl + phase_result mechanism.
The PerformerCompletionKind enum (5 variants) and CanonicalClass enum (13 variants) are the extension points for error granularity.
Existing tests (312+ core tests) must continue passing after each task.
The supervisor agent is a new binary/process that runs alongside the coordinator, not embedded inside it.
Git operations go through core/src/git.rs; new git helpers (tag, log inspection) follow existing patterns.
The PRD reconciliation flow (sync-prd, audit-prd) uses commit message conventions with [macc:task TASK-ID] tags.

tasks.title: Define IPC-over-exit-code priority contract and types
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The completion classifier in engine.rs allows exit-code heuristics to override IPC phase_done signals, causing tasks with committed work to be wrongly marked as errors.
Key actions: Define a CompletionAuthority enum (IpcSignal, ExitCodeHeuristic, Fallback). Add a resolution function that returns IPC result when IPC reported phase_done AND worktree has commits ahead of base, regardless of exit code. Document the priority inversion contract.
Out of scope: Changing the IPC transport itself. Modifying performer scripts.
Success criteria: A clear type and resolution function exist that encode the rule: IPC + commits = phase_done, period. Unit tests cover all authority combinations.
tasks.objective: Establish the type contract for IPC-over-exit-code priority so downstream classifier changes are safe and testable.
tasks.result: New CompletionAuthority enum and resolve_completion_authority() function in coordinator module with full unit test coverage.
steps: Create CompletionAuthority enum with variants: IpcSignal, ExitCodeHeuristic, Fallback.
Implement resolve_completion_authority() that checks: (1) IPC phase_result present, (2) commits ahead of base, (3) exit code.
Write unit tests for all combinations: IPC+commits, IPC+no-commits, no-IPC+exit-success, no-IPC+exit-failure.
Document the priority inversion contract in code comments.
tasks.notes: This is the contracts-first task for Recommendation 1. The actual classifier integration depends on this.

tasks.title: Integrate IPC-over-exit-code priority into completion classifier
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The completion classifier in engine.rs (lines 823-960) must use the new CompletionAuthority resolution instead of allowing exit-code to override IPC signals.
Key actions: Refactor the success/error classification paths in engine.rs to call resolve_completion_authority() first. When authority is IpcSignal and IPC reported phase_done with commits, set completion to phase_done regardless of input.success flag. Preserve existing behavior when no IPC signal was received.
Out of scope: Changing how IPC signals are collected. Modifying the PerformerCompletionKind enum.
Success criteria: A task that reports phase_done via IPC with commits ahead of base is classified as phase_done even if the process exit code is non-zero. Existing tests pass. New integration tests cover the override scenario.
tasks.objective: Eliminate the priority inversion where exit-code heuristics override IPC phase_done signals.
tasks.result: engine.rs completion classifier uses resolve_completion_authority(). Tasks with IPC phase_done + commits are never downgraded to error_with_changes.
steps: In engine.rs, replace the direct input.success check with resolve_completion_authority() call.
When authority is IpcSignal and completion_kind is phase_done, skip the exit-code error path entirely.
Add a git::commits_ahead_of_base() helper if not already present (or reuse existing branch inspection).
Write integration test: simulate IPC phase_done + non-zero exit + commits ahead → verify phase_done outcome.
Write regression test: no IPC signal + non-zero exit → verify error classification preserved.
tasks.notes: This is the most impactful single fix. It directly prevents the 'committed work abandoned and redone' failure mode.

tasks.title: Extend error code taxonomy with granular sub-codes
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: Current error codes (E101-E901) don't distinguish error source and severity well enough. A git failure, a performer tool crash, and a post-commit error all need different retry strategies.
Key actions: Add new sub-codes within existing ranges: E104 (performer partial changes), E105 (performer complete but exit non-zero), E304 (worktree branch conflict), E305 (worktree checkout failure), E306 (worktree reset failure), E403 (task state conflict), E503 (merge blocked by policy), E504 (post-merge validation failed). Extend CanonicalClass if needed. Update error_normalizer.rs mapping table.
Out of scope: Changing the error normalization pipeline architecture. Adding new E-ranges.
Success criteria: Each new code has a clear definition, maps to a CanonicalClass, and has a documented retry policy (retryable/not-retryable/conditional).
tasks.objective: Provide error granularity that enables differentiated retry and recovery strategies.
tasks.result: error_normalizer.rs has new sub-codes with mappings. Documentation in code comments describes each code's semantics and retry policy.
steps: Add E104, E105 to E100 range in error code constants.
Add E304, E305, E306 to E300 range.
Add E403 to E400 range.
Add E503, E504 to E500 range.
Update the error code → CanonicalClass mapping table.
Add GitConflict and PostCommitFailure to CanonicalClass if not already represented.
Update README.md error code documentation section.
Write unit tests verifying each new code maps to the correct class.
tasks.notes: This task is a contracts-first dependency for salvage, retry-on-same-worktree, and merge-gate tasks. Keep backward compatibility — existing codes must not change meaning.

tasks.title: Add git helpers for branch inspection and tagging
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: Salvage, merge-gate, and branch-aware abandonment all need git operations not yet in git.rs: checking commits ahead of base with message filtering, creating lightweight tags, listing branches by pattern.
Key actions: Add commits_ahead_of_base(worktree, base_branch) → Vec<CommitInfo>. Add commits_containing_pattern(worktree, base_branch, pattern) → Vec<CommitInfo>. Add create_tag(repo, tag_name, commit_ref). Add list_branches_by_prefix(repo, prefix). Add async variants for all.
Out of scope: Changing existing git.rs functions. Adding libgit2 dependency.
Success criteria: All new helpers have unit tests. Async variants exist for coordinator use. Functions follow existing git.rs patterns (run_git_status / Command::new).
tasks.objective: Provide the git building blocks needed by salvage, merge-gate, abandonment, and sync-unmerged tasks.
tasks.result: git.rs has new functions: commits_ahead_of_base, commits_containing_pattern, create_tag, create_tag_async, list_branches_by_prefix, list_branches_by_prefix_async with tests.
steps: Implement commits_ahead_of_base() using git log base..HEAD --oneline.
Implement commits_containing_pattern() using git log --grep=<pattern> base..HEAD.
Implement create_tag() using git tag <name> <ref>.
Implement list_branches_by_prefix() using git branch --list <prefix>*.
Add async variants using tokio::process::Command following existing patterns.
Write unit tests using temporary git repos (follow existing test patterns in git.rs).
tasks.notes: CommitInfo struct should include hash, subject, author_date at minimum. Keep it simple — these are plumbing functions.

tasks.title: Implement pre-retry salvage check in coordinator
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: Before retrying a failed task, the coordinator should check if the previous worktree/branch has mergeable committed work. If so, attempt merge instead of wasting a retry.
Key actions: Add salvage_check() function that: (1) resolves the task's previous worktree/branch from registry metadata, (2) calls commits_containing_pattern() to find task-ID commits ahead of base, (3) if found, attempts merge of the branch, (4) if merge succeeds → mark task merged and skip retry, (5) if merge fails (conflicts) → proceed with retry, (6) if no relevant commits → proceed with retry normally.
Out of scope: Modifying the merge worker itself. Handling multi-phase task salvage.
Success criteria: Tasks with committed work on orphaned branches are salvaged before retry. Salvage attempts are logged in coordinator events. Failed salvage proceeds to normal retry without blocking.
tasks.objective: Recover committed work from failed tasks instead of redoing work from scratch.
tasks.result: New salvage_check() function integrated into the retry path in engine.rs. Coordinator events log salvage attempts and outcomes.
steps: Add task_runtime metadata field: last_worktree_path and last_branch (populated before clearing task.worktree on error).
Implement salvage_check(task, registry, config) → SalvageResult { Merged, ConflictProceedRetry, NoCommitsProceedRetry }.
In the retry path of engine.rs, call salvage_check() before dispatching a new performer.
If SalvageResult::Merged, transition task to merged and emit salvage_success event.
If SalvageResult::ConflictProceedRetry or NoCommitsProceedRetry, continue with normal retry.
Emit coordinator events for all salvage outcomes.
Write unit tests for each SalvageResult path.
Write integration test: task with commits on orphaned branch → salvage merges → task done.
tasks.notes: This is Recommendation 2. Depends on git helpers for branch inspection and the error code taxonomy for classifying salvage-specific failures.

tasks.title: Implement retry-on-same-worktree strategy
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: When a task fails with committed changes (error_with_changes), the current behavior clears task.worktree = None and retries on a fresh worker, losing all committed progress. The retry should prefer the same worktree when the task has committed work.
Key actions: Refactor the error_with_changes handling path in engine.rs (lines 833-854) to: (1) check if original worktree is still available and healthy, (2) if yes AND task has commits → keep task.worktree, reset to todo for retry on same worktree, (3) if original worktree gone/occupied → fall back to new worktree + salvage attempt, (4) error_no_changes → clear task.worktree = None (preserve current behavior).
Out of scope: Changing the worktree pool allocation logic. Modifying performer behavior.
Success criteria: Tasks with error_with_changes retry on the same worktree preserving commits. Tasks with error_no_changes get a fresh worktree. Worktree health check prevents retrying on a corrupt slot.
tasks.objective: Preserve committed progress by retrying on the same worktree when possible.
tasks.result: engine.rs error_with_changes path checks worktree availability and preserves task.worktree when commits exist. New worktree health check function.
steps: Add is_worktree_healthy(path) check: exists, is git worktree, no lock files, no rebase/merge in progress.
In error_with_changes handler, check is_worktree_healthy(task.worktree).
If healthy + commits ahead → keep task.worktree, set task state to todo with retry reason.
If unhealthy or no commits → clear task.worktree = None (existing behavior), trigger salvage path.
Ensure the dispatch phase recognizes a task with pre-assigned worktree and skips pool allocation.
Write tests for: healthy worktree retained, unhealthy worktree cleared, no-changes worktree cleared.
Write integration test: error_with_changes + healthy worktree → same slot reused on retry.
tasks.notes: This is Recommendation 3. Must coordinate with salvage (L4-SALVAGE-001) for the fallback path when worktree is gone.

tasks.title: Implement branch-aware abandonment with tagging
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: When a worktree slot is recycled, committed work on the old branch is silently lost. Before abandoning a branch, the coordinator should preserve the work with a tag.
Key actions: Before resetting a worktree slot (in helpers.rs prepare_reused_worktree_base and stuck-branch abandon path): (1) check if the current branch has commits ahead of base, (2) if yes, create a lightweight tag: macc/abandoned/TASK-ID-<timestamp>, (3) log the tag creation in coordinator events, (4) then proceed with branch reset/detach.
Out of scope: Automatic cleanup of old tags. Adding tag-based recovery to the CLI.
Success criteria: No committed work is silently lost. Tags are created before branch reset. Tags follow a consistent naming convention searchable by task ID.
tasks.objective: Ensure committed work is never silently destroyed when worktree slots are recycled.
tasks.result: helpers.rs abandon paths create macc/abandoned/ tags before resetting. Coordinator events log tag creation.
steps: In helpers.rs, before the branch reset in prepare_reused_worktree_base(), check commits_ahead_of_base().
If commits exist, resolve the task ID from the branch name or worktree metadata.
Create tag: macc/abandoned/<task-id>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS> pointing to current HEAD.
Log tag creation as a coordinator event.
Repeat for the stuck-branch abandon path (~line 221 in helpers.rs).
Write unit test: worktree with commits → tag created before reset.
Write unit test: worktree with no commits → no tag created, normal reset.
tasks.notes: This is Recommendation 5. Uses git helpers from L4-GIT-001. Simple and high-value safety net.

tasks.title: Implement merge-gate before retry dispatch
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: Even with salvage, there's a window where a task gets dispatched for retry while its previous branch has mergeable work. A merge-gate check at dispatch time prevents double-work.
Key actions: In the dispatch phase (control_plane.rs), before launching a performer for a retried task: (1) check if any branch matching the task ID pattern exists, (2) if found and has commits ahead of base, attempt a fast-forward or clean merge, (3) if merge succeeds → cancel dispatch, mark task merged, (4) if merge fails → proceed with dispatch.
Out of scope: Changing the merge worker conflict resolution. Adding merge policies.
Success criteria: No task is dispatched for retry if its previous branch can be cleanly merged. Merge-gate attempts are logged.
tasks.objective: Last-chance check before retry dispatch to prevent redoing already-committed work.
tasks.result: control_plane.rs dispatch phase includes merge_gate_check() for retried tasks. Successful merge-gate cancels dispatch.
steps: Implement merge_gate_check(task_id, base_branch, repo_path) → MergeGateResult { Merged, ConflictProceed, NoBranchProceed }.
Use list_branches_by_prefix() to find branches matching the task ID.
For each matching branch, check commits_ahead_of_base().
Attempt git merge --ff-only or git merge --no-edit for clean merges.
In dispatch phase, call merge_gate_check() when task.retry_count > 0.
If Merged → transition task to merged, emit event, skip dispatch.
Write tests for each MergeGateResult path.
tasks.notes: This is Recommendation 6. Works as a safety net complementing salvage (L4-SALVAGE-001). Lightweight check that prevents the most visible failure mode.

tasks.title: Reconcile unmerged task branches during sync phase
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The sync phase (sync-prd) only looks at the reference branch for merged commits. Unmerged branches with completed work are invisible, causing tasks to be retried unnecessarily.
Key actions: Add a sync_unmerged_branches() step to the sync phase that: (1) lists all branches matching macc/worker-* or task ID patterns, (2) for each, checks if commits contain [macc:task TASK-ID] tags, (3) for tasks still in todo/error state, attempt merge, (4) if merge succeeds → transition to merged, (5) if merge fails → log and skip (operator can resolve later).
Out of scope: Changing the existing sync-prd commit scanning logic. Handling complex merge conflicts.
Success criteria: The sync phase discovers and merges orphaned task branches. Tasks with mergeable orphaned branches are transitioned to merged during sync.
tasks.objective: Make the sync phase aware of unmerged task branches so completed work is not invisible.
tasks.result: Sync phase includes sync_unmerged_branches() that discovers and merges orphaned task branches. New coordinator events for branch discovery and merge outcomes.
steps: Implement sync_unmerged_branches(registry, repo_path, base_branch) → Vec<SyncBranchResult>.
List branches matching known patterns (macc/worker-*, task ID prefixes).
For each branch, scan commit messages for [macc:task TASK-ID] tags.
Cross-reference found task IDs with registry — filter to tasks in todo/error states.
Attempt merge for each candidate branch.
On success: transition task to merged, emit event.
On failure: log conflict, emit event, skip.
Integrate into the sync phase pipeline after existing sync-prd step.
Write tests covering: orphaned branch found and merged, orphaned branch with conflicts skipped, no orphaned branches.
tasks.notes: This is Recommendation 7. Complements sync-prd which only scans the reference branch. Together they form a complete reconciliation pipeline.

tasks.title: Add coordinator config fields for new reliability features
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The new salvage, retry-on-same-worktree, merge-gate, and abandonment features need configuration toggles and thresholds in CoordinatorConfig.
Key actions: Add fields to CoordinatorConfig in config/mod.rs: salvage_before_retry (bool, default true), retry_on_same_worktree (bool, default true), merge_gate_on_dispatch (bool, default true), tag_abandoned_branches (bool, default true), sync_unmerged_branches (bool, default true), salvage_merge_timeout_seconds (u64, default 120), max_salvage_attempts_per_task (u32, default 1). Add corresponding YAML keys under automation.coordinator.
Out of scope: Adding TUI screens for these settings. Changing existing config fields.
Success criteria: New config fields are loaded from macc.yaml, have sensible defaults, and are accessible by coordinator engine/helpers.
tasks.objective: Expose configuration for all new reliability features with safe defaults.
tasks.result: CoordinatorConfig has new fields. macc.yaml supports new keys under automation.coordinator. Default values enable all reliability features.
steps: Add fields to CoordinatorConfig struct in config/mod.rs.
Set default values using Default trait implementation.
Add YAML deserialization support for new keys.
Write test: default config has all features enabled.
Write test: config from YAML with overrides is correctly loaded.
Update config documentation in docs/CONFIG.md.
tasks.notes: This is a cross-cutting config task. Keep it focused on adding fields — the features themselves are in separate tasks.

tasks.title: Add coordinator event kinds for salvage, merge-gate, and abandonment
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: New reliability features need observable events in the coordinator event bus for monitoring, debugging, and TUI live display.
Key actions: Add event kinds to CoordinatorRuntimeEventKind: SalvageAttempted, SalvageMerged, SalvageFailed, MergeGateChecked, MergeGateMerged, BranchTaggedAbandoned, SyncUnmergedBranchFound, SyncUnmergedBranchMerged, WorktreeHealthCheckFailed. Ensure each event carries relevant metadata (task_id, branch, worktree_path, outcome).
Out of scope: Changing the event bus transport. Modifying TUI event rendering (separate task).
Success criteria: All new features emit structured events. Events are written to events.jsonl. Event kinds are documented.
tasks.objective: Make all new reliability operations observable through the coordinator event bus.
tasks.result: CoordinatorRuntimeEventKind has new variants. Events are emitted by salvage, merge-gate, abandonment, and sync-unmerged features.
steps: Add new variants to CoordinatorRuntimeEventKind enum in runtime.rs.
Define metadata fields for each event kind.
Ensure serialization to events.jsonl works for new variants.
Write unit tests verifying event serialization roundtrip.
Document event kinds in code comments.
tasks.notes: This is a preparatory task that other tasks depend on for event emission. Keep the event definitions stable.

tasks.title: Update README and MACC.md with reliability features documentation
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The new reliability features (salvage, retry-on-same-worktree, merge-gate, abandonment tagging, sync-unmerged, granular error codes) need user-facing documentation.
Key actions: Update README.md error code table with new sub-codes. Add a 'Coordinator Recovery & Reliability' section to MACC.md describing salvage, merge-gate, and abandonment behaviors. Update the auto-retry policy section with new retry strategies. Document new config keys.
Out of scope: Writing developer/contributor docs for implementation internals. Updating TUI help text.
Success criteria: A user reading the docs understands the new recovery behaviors, can configure them, and knows what the new error codes mean.
tasks.objective: Document all new reliability features for users and operators.
tasks.result: README.md and MACC.md have updated sections covering new error codes, recovery features, and configuration keys.
steps: Add new error sub-codes (E104, E105, E304-E306, E403, E503-E504) to README.md error code table.
Add 'Coordinator Recovery & Reliability' section to MACC.md.
Document salvage-before-retry behavior and its config toggle.
Document retry-on-same-worktree behavior.
Document merge-gate-on-dispatch behavior.
Document branch-aware abandonment and tag naming convention.
Document sync-unmerged-branches during sync phase.
Update auto-retry policy section in README.md.
Document new config keys in docs/CONFIG.md.
tasks.notes: Should be done after the implementation tasks are complete so documentation matches actual behavior.

tasks.title: Define supervisor agent contract and communication protocol
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The supervisor agent needs a clear contract for how it communicates with and monitors the coordinator. This includes: process lifecycle management, health check protocol, event consumption, and report format.
Key actions: Define SupervisorConfig struct (watchdog interval, max_restart_attempts, log_analysis_window, report_output_path). Define HealthCheckResult enum (Healthy, Degraded, Unresponsive, Crashed). Define SupervisorReport struct (timestamp, findings, recommendations, actions_taken, suggested_code_changes). Define the coordinator process management interface (start, stop, health-check, pid tracking). Define event consumption interface (tail events.jsonl, parse known event kinds).
Out of scope: Implementing the AI analysis logic. Building the full supervisor binary.
Success criteria: Clear types and traits exist for supervisor-coordinator communication. Report format is structured and machine-readable. Health check protocol is specified.
tasks.objective: Establish the foundational types and contracts for the supervisor agent.
tasks.result: New module core/src/supervisor/ with types: SupervisorConfig, HealthCheckResult, SupervisorReport, SupervisorAction, ProcessManager trait.
steps: Create core/src/supervisor/mod.rs with module structure.
Define SupervisorConfig with all configuration fields and defaults.
Define HealthCheckResult enum: Healthy, Degraded(reasons), Unresponsive, Crashed(exit_code).
Define SupervisorReport struct with: timestamp, analysis_window, findings (Vec<Finding>), recommendations (Vec<Recommendation>), actions_taken (Vec<Action>), suggested_code_changes (Vec<CodeChange>).
Define Finding struct: severity, category, description, evidence (log excerpts, event data).
Define Recommendation struct: priority, description, rationale, affected_files, implementation_hint.
Define CodeChange struct: file_path, description, before_context, suggested_change.
Define ProcessManager trait: start_coordinator(), stop_coordinator(), health_check(), coordinator_pid().
Write unit tests for type serialization/deserialization.
Document the communication protocol in code comments.
tasks.notes: This is the contracts-first task for Recommendation 8 (Supervisor Agent). All supervisor implementation tasks depend on this. The report format must be detailed enough to generate actionable MACC source code changes.

tasks.title: Implement supervisor Mode A: watchdog and health monitoring
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The supervisor needs to detect when the coordinator is unhealthy, stuck, or has crashed. Mode A is the always-on watchdog layer.
Key actions: Implement coordinator process monitoring (pid file tracking, process liveness check). Implement event stream monitoring (tail events.jsonl, detect stalled event emission). Implement health check logic: no events for N seconds = Degraded, process gone = Crashed, repeated error events = Degraded. Implement basic alerting (log warnings, write health status file).
Out of scope: AI-powered analysis (Mode B/C). Automatic restart (Mode C). Report generation.
Success criteria: Supervisor detects coordinator crash within watchdog interval. Supervisor detects stalled coordinator (no events) within configured threshold. Health status is written to a file readable by CLI/TUI.
tasks.objective: Provide continuous health monitoring of the coordinator process.
tasks.result: Supervisor watchdog loop monitors coordinator process and event stream. Health status written to .macc/state/supervisor-health.json.
steps: Implement ProcessManager for coordinator: start/stop/health via pid file and process signals.
Implement event stream tailer: follow events.jsonl, parse last event timestamp.
Implement health evaluation: compare last event time to watchdog interval, check process liveness.
Write health status to .macc/state/supervisor-health.json on each check cycle.
Implement configurable watchdog interval (default 30s).
Write tests: healthy coordinator detected, stalled coordinator detected, crashed coordinator detected.
tasks.notes: Mode A runs continuously as a background loop. It's the foundation for Modes B and C. Keep it lightweight — no AI calls in this mode.

tasks.title: Implement supervisor Mode B: worktree recovery with AI analysis
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: When a worktree is stuck or a task has failed in an unexpected way, the supervisor should use an AI performer to analyze logs and attempt recovery while the coordinator continues running.
Key actions: Implement log collection for a failed/stuck worktree (performer logs, coordinator events for that task, git status, branch state). Build a structured prompt for AI analysis that includes: collected evidence, known error patterns, expected outcome format. Dispatch AI performer to a dedicated supervisor worktree for analysis. Parse AI response into SupervisorReport. If the report includes a recovery action (e.g., resolve conflict, reset state), execute it. Write the report to .macc/log/supervisor/.
Out of scope: Modifying the coordinator's running state directly. Implementing Mode C (coordinator restart). Complex multi-step recovery chains.
Success criteria: Supervisor can analyze a stuck worktree using an AI performer. AI report is structured and actionable. Recovery actions are attempted when safe. All actions are logged.
tasks.objective: Enable AI-powered analysis and recovery of stuck worktrees without stopping the coordinator.
tasks.result: Supervisor Mode B collects evidence, dispatches AI analysis, parses reports, and attempts safe recovery actions. Reports written to .macc/log/supervisor/.
steps: Implement evidence_collector: gather performer logs, coordinator events, git status, branch diff for a target worktree.
Build structured AI prompt template with: evidence, known error patterns, expected response format (JSON matching SupervisorReport).
Implement AI performer dispatch using existing performer infrastructure (reuse performer.sh + tool runner).
Parse AI response into SupervisorReport struct.
Implement safe recovery actions: git reset, branch cleanup, task state reset (only actions that don't affect other tasks).
Write report to .macc/log/supervisor/<task-id>-<timestamp>.json.
Add guard rails: max one recovery attempt per task per supervisor cycle, timeout on AI analysis.
Write tests: evidence collection, prompt construction, report parsing, safe action execution.
tasks.notes: Mode B is the first AI-powered supervisor mode. It runs in parallel with the coordinator. Critical constraint: it must not modify coordinator state directly — only worktree-level recovery is safe.

tasks.title: Implement supervisor Mode C: coordinator restart and recovery
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: When the coordinator itself crashes or exits unexpectedly, the supervisor must be able to restart it and ensure the task registry is consistent before resumption.
Key actions: Detect coordinator exit via watchdog (Mode A). Before restart: (1) collect crash evidence (last events, exit code, stderr), (2) validate task registry consistency (no tasks stuck in claimed/in_progress without active performers), (3) reset stuck tasks to todo, (4) save session snapshot, (5) restart coordinator process. After restart: verify coordinator is healthy via watchdog. Generate a crash recovery report.
Out of scope: AI-powered crash root cause analysis (can be added later by combining with Mode B). Automatic code fixes.
Success criteria: Supervisor restarts coordinator after crash within configured max_restart_attempts. Task registry is cleaned up before restart. No tasks are permanently stuck due to coordinator crash. Crash recovery report is generated.
tasks.objective: Enable automatic coordinator recovery after crashes with clean state restoration.
tasks.result: Supervisor Mode C detects coordinator exit, cleans registry, restarts coordinator, and generates crash recovery report.
steps: In watchdog loop, detect coordinator process exit (Crashed health check result).
Implement pre-restart cleanup: scan registry for tasks in claimed/in_progress, check if their performer processes are still running.
Reset orphaned tasks (claimed/in_progress with no active performer) to todo state.
Call session save before restart (preserve session continuity).
Restart coordinator via ProcessManager::start_coordinator().
After restart, run health checks for N cycles to confirm recovery.
If restart fails max_restart_attempts times, write critical alert and stop.
Generate crash recovery report with: crash evidence, cleanup actions, restart outcome.
Write report to .macc/log/supervisor/crash-recovery-<timestamp>.json.
Write tests: crash detected and restarted, registry cleanup before restart, max restarts exceeded.
tasks.notes: Mode C is the most critical supervisor capability. It makes the coordinator self-healing for crash scenarios. Keep the restart logic simple and deterministic — no AI in the restart path itself.

tasks.title: Implement supervisor feedback loop and actionable report generation
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: Supervisor reports must be developer-actionable — clear enough that a developer can use them to modify MACC source code to handle the observed failure permanently. The feedback loop aggregates patterns across runs.
Key actions: Implement report aggregation: collect individual reports from Mode B/C, identify recurring patterns (same error, same file, same worktree symptom). Generate aggregated reports with: pattern frequency, affected code paths, concrete suggested changes (file, function, before/after). Store aggregated reports in .macc/log/supervisor/aggregated/. Implement a CLI command to view supervisor reports: macc supervisor report [--latest|--list|--id <id>].
Out of scope: Automatically applying code changes. Integrating with CI/CD.
Success criteria: Aggregated reports identify recurring failure patterns. Each pattern includes actionable code change suggestions with file paths and function names. CLI command provides easy access to reports.
tasks.objective: Turn supervisor observations into actionable developer insights for permanent MACC improvements.
tasks.result: Aggregated supervisor reports with code change suggestions. CLI command for report access. Reports stored in .macc/log/supervisor/aggregated/.
steps: Implement report aggregation: scan .macc/log/supervisor/ for individual reports.
Group findings by error pattern (error code, affected file, symptom description).
For each recurring pattern, generate a CodeChange suggestion with: file_path, function_name, description, implementation_hint.
Write aggregated report to .macc/log/supervisor/aggregated/<timestamp>.json.
Add CLI command: macc supervisor report --latest (show latest aggregated report).
Add CLI command: macc supervisor report --list (list all reports).
Add CLI command: macc supervisor report --id <id> (show specific report).
Write tests: aggregation logic, pattern grouping, CLI command routing.
tasks.notes: This is the feedback loop that closes the supervisor cycle. Reports should be structured enough to be consumed by both humans and potentially by an AI code modification tool.

tasks.title: Add supervisor CLI commands and config integration
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The supervisor agent needs CLI entry points for starting, stopping, and configuring it. It also needs integration with macc.yaml for persistent configuration.
Key actions: Add CLI commands: macc supervisor start [--daemon], macc supervisor stop, macc supervisor status, macc supervisor report. Add SupervisorConfig to macc.yaml under automation.supervisor. Add supervisor config fields to CoordinatorConfig or create a sibling config section. Wire CLI commands to supervisor process management.
Out of scope: TUI integration for supervisor. Web UI supervisor dashboard.
Success criteria: Supervisor can be started/stopped via CLI. Configuration is loaded from macc.yaml. Status command shows supervisor health and coordinator health.
tasks.objective: Provide CLI and configuration entry points for the supervisor agent.

tasks.title: End-to-end integration test for coordinator reliability features
tasks.description:
Problem/Goal: The individual reliability features need an integration test that validates the full coordinator cycle with the new behaviors.
Key actions: Create an integration test scenario that exercises: (1) IPC phase_done with non-zero exit → phase_done (not error), (2) error_with_changes → retry on same worktree, (3) abandoned branch gets tagged before recycling, (4) orphaned branch discovered during sync and merged, (5) merge-gate prevents duplicate dispatch. Use mock performers and a test git repository.
Out of scope: Testing the supervisor agent (separate test suite). Performance benchmarks.
Success criteria: A single integration test validates the complete reliability improvement chain. Test runs in CI.
tasks.objective: Validate that all coordinator reliability features work together correctly.
tasks.result: Integration test in tests/ that exercises the full reliability feature chain with mock performers and test git repos.
steps: Set up test harness: temporary git repo, test task registry, mock performer that simulates IPC + exit codes.
Test scenario 1: performer reports phase_done via IPC, exits non-zero → verify task transitions to phase_done.
Test scenario 2: performer fails with committed changes → verify retry on same worktree.
Test scenario 3: worktree recycled with commits → verify abandoned tag created.
Test scenario 4: orphaned branch with task commits → verify sync discovers and merges.
Test scenario 5: retried task with mergeable previous branch → verify merge-gate prevents dispatch.
Ensure all scenarios run independently and clean up after themselves.
Add to CI test suite.
tasks.notes: This is the validation capstone for the reliability improvements. Should be the last implementation task before documentation.
